METADATA.title: How Much Does A Refinish Hurt A Vintage Guitar's Value?
METADATA.description: A full refinish means 40 to 60 percent less than a comparable original. I'll explain Gibson and Fender comparisons, partial work and factory refinishes.

mainEntity.name: How Much Does A Full Refinish Lower Value?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full refinish generally means 40 to 60 percent less than a comparable original. Compare the same model and period with similar parts, wear and structural condition.

mainEntity.name: Does A Professional Refinish Avoid The Loss?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. A professional full refinish still generally means 40 to 60 percent less than a comparable original. Good workmanship helps preserve the remaining instrument, but it doesn't replace the first finish.

mainEntity.name: Is Overspray The Same As A Full Refinish?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Overspray adds finish over an existing surface, while a full refinish may remove or replace much more material. The extent of the work and what survives underneath need to be established before making a comparison.

mainEntity.name: Does A Custom Color Repaint Add The Original Color Premium?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. A later custom-color repaint doesn't establish that the guitar left the factory in that color. Compare it with its actual original specification and describe the later finish clearly.

mainEntity.name: Is A Fender Factory Refinish Original Finish?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. A factory refinish is later work by Fender. Its documentation and repair-department evidence can distinguish it from an aftermarket repaint, but it is still different from the guitar's first finish.
